notes: The image's breadboard shows rows j-f on the top half and e-a on the bottom half; the catalogue says bank 't' = rows a-e and 'b' = rows f-j. I used the row letters from the image with the bank that matches the letter, so rows f-j are 'b' and rows a-e are 't'. Strip membership is unchanged, because the button straddles the centre gap.
Breadboard columns were read from the image. The button legs are in columns 4 and 6, the resistor spans columns 6 to 9, the teal wire is at 6b.i and the black wire is at column 9.
Rail hole numbers (bp.2, bp.4, bn.2, bn.9) are estimates from the picture. Only the rail they are on matters electrically.
The lower rail's top line (black) is the ground rail 'bn' and its red line is the 5V rail 'bp'.
The pushbutton's two sides are the two columns. Column 6 (top and bottom legs) is side 1 and goes to pin 2 and the pull-down resistor. Column 4 is side 2 and goes to 5V through the orange wire.
The 10k pull-down resistor goes from column 6 (the pin 2 side) to column 9, and a black wire takes column 9 to the GND rail.
The LED is the built-in LED on pin 13, so there is no external LED. The Uno's GND.1 is used for the ground wire.
